questions.question: Rewrite using the correct tense: 'When I (reach) the station, the train already (leave).'
questions.solution:
**When I reached the station, the train had already left.**

Rule: past perfect ('had left') shows the earlier of two past actions; simple past ('reached') shows the later one.

questions.question: Combine into a complex sentence: 'He is very poor. He is honest.'
questions.solution:
**Although he is very poor, he is honest.**

(Also acceptable: *Though he is very poor, he is honest.* — subordinating conjunction introduces the dependent clause.)

questions.question: Write a letter to your friend describing how you spent your last vacation.
questions.solution:
Model answer (informal letter format):

Kathmandu
15 March 2024

Dear Anita,
I hope you are fine. I am writing to tell you about my vacation. During the holidays I visited Pokhara with my family. We boated on Phewa Lake, watched the sunrise from Sarangkot and trekked part of the way to Australian Camp. The mountain views were breathtaking. Besides sightseeing, I finished two novels and helped my mother in the garden. It was refreshing after months of study.
Give my regards to your parents.

Yours lovingly,
Sita

questions.question: What is the difference between 'few' and 'a few'?
questions.solution:
**Few** = hardly any; has a negative sense (not enough). E.g. He has few friends (almost no friends).

**A few** = some; positive sense (at least some). E.g. He has a few friends (some friends).
